doc.interviewee: Mrs. Charlotte Botney and Mrs. Bertha George McCullum

title: Joe Oliver goes to Chicago; George's own bands
summary: Joe Oliver went up to Chicago and stayed; she knew him from her house before he married, and George had his own string and brass bands.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: He went up there on physical. Quite a few of the bands were like Joe Oliver, you know, went up there while the guys stayed. Joe went up there all the time and stayed. Joe just had his wife and when Joe left, you know, I don't know if he and his wife was together.
They stayed together quite a while. They stayed together. I think they finally did separate in late years. When he died, Joe was over in Savannah. She was back here.

I didn't know too much about her, but I knew him long before he ever got married because he was in my house all the time with my husband. All those young boys. And most of them weren't married. No. As I say, they'd just flock and that's all he was, his work and his music too.
Most of the time he had his own band. Most of the time.
The string band and his brass band.
